title: C55 crop and resampler register reference

registers.name: Pipeline: Bypass crop
registers.validation: Must be 0 or 1; bypass takes precedence over enable.

registers.name: Crop: Enable crop
registers.validation: Must be 0 or 1; crop operates only when bypass=0 and enable=1.

registers.name: Crop: start x
registers.description: Horizontal margin removed from the left side.
registers.validation: Active crop must fit inside the actual input frame.
registers.status: Geometry ignored when crop is inactive

registers.name: Crop: start y
registers.description: Vertical margin removed from the top side.
registers.validation: Active crop must fit inside the actual input frame.
registers.status: Geometry ignored when crop is inactive

registers.name: Crop: size x
registers.validation: Active crop must fit; effective scaler width must be divisible by 8.
registers.status: Geometry ignored when crop is inactive

registers.name: Crop: size y
registers.validation: Active crop must fit; effective scaler height must be divisible by 8.
registers.status: Geometry ignored when crop is inactive

registers.name: vfilt_tinc
registers.description: Vertical input height divided by output height, in 4.20 format.
registers.known_width: 4.20 numeric format; storage width not specified
registers.validation: Must equal (height_in << 20) // oheight; slide ratio limits also apply.

registers.name: height_in
registers.description: Height of the frame entering the scaler.
registers.validation: Must equal effective crop height, or actual frame height when crop is inactive.

registers.name: oheight
registers.validation: Explicit output dimension; no automatic output-size rounding.

registers.name: vfilt_coefset
registers.description: Select one of 16 vertical scaler coefficient sets.
registers.allowed_values: Hardware selector: 0-15; model supports only software bank 0
registers.validation: Zero selects the PC-generated software bilinear bank; nonzero rejected. Hardware bank contents are not inferred.
registers.status: Active for bilinear; validated but unused for nearest/average

registers.name: hfilt_tinc
registers.description: Horizontal input width divided by output width, in 4.20 format.
registers.known_width: 4.20 numeric format; storage width not specified
registers.validation: Must equal (width_in << 20) // owidth; screenshot says heights, an apparent typo.

registers.name: width_in
registers.description: Width of the frame entering the scaler.
registers.validation: Must equal effective crop width, or actual frame width when crop is inactive.

registers.name: owidth
registers.validation: Explicit output dimension; no automatic output-size rounding.

registers.name: hfilt_coefset
registers.description: Select one of 16 horizontal scaler coefficient sets.
registers.allowed_values: Hardware selector: 0-15; model supports only software bank 0
registers.validation: Zero selects the PC-generated software bilinear bank; nonzero rejected. Hardware bank contents are not inferred.
registers.status: Active for bilinear; validated but unused for nearest/average

registers.name: Resampler: method
registers.validation: Only the three listed integers are accepted.

registers.name: Resampler: interpolation
registers.description: Select the register-driven coordinate mapping for all methods.
registers.validation: With s=T/2^20: original x=u*s; shift x=(u+1/2)*s-1/2; likewise vertically.

notes.text: Register names and descriptions come from the supplied Crop and Down scaler screenshots. The Resampler slide supplies the divisibility-by-8 and output/input ratio [1/8, 7/8] limits. The boundary document proposes consistency and edge policies; it does not establish exact C55 hardware behavior. Validation rules and software controls here are the adopted wrapper contract.

This version accepts only nonempty uint8 RGB arrays with three full-resolution channels and RGB image files. Eventual pipeline input will be YUV. YUV is not interchangeable with RGB; layout, chroma subsampling, range and conversion must be specified during future integration. No YUV conversion is implemented.

C55 uses its local row-streaming implementation. The PC-generated software bank has 32 phases and seven signed 8-bit slots, with weights [0,0,0,64-2*p,2*p,0,0] at phase p. Horizontal sums retain scale 64; vertical sums retain scale 4096 until final nearest-even rounding and uint8 saturation. The independent ocr_bench.resample benchmark kernel is unchanged. This integer processing contract is not verified C55 hardware arithmetic.

Unsigned Q4.20 increments are checked against truncated integer division and drive sampling. Q21 coordinate state advances by 2*T, initialized to zero for original mapping or T-2^20 for shift. Dimensions determine bounds and output count. No undocumented hardware address, storage width, or dimension maximum is assigned.

For s=T/2^20, original samples x=u*s and shift samples x=(u+1/2)*s-1/2. Bilinear quantizes the fractional coordinate to 32 phases using nearest-even rounding; phase 32 carries into the base and becomes phase 0, without altering accumulator state. Nearest rounds the unquantized coordinate half up. Average uses unquantized floor/floor+1 neighbors and (sum+2)//4, not area averaging. Clamp selected neighbors to the effective crop edge and process RGB channels independently.

All 16 fields are required integers (booleans excluded). Unknown and duplicate JSON keys are rejected. Inactive crop geometry is ignored after type validation. Setup and coefficients are latched before input consumption. The row API validates frame_shape and every input row, including cropped-out and trailing rows; short, extra, or malformed rows fail. Output is provisional until successful iterator exhaustion. The array adapter and image CLI collect the same streaming implementation.

Both effective scaler input dimensions must be divisible by 8, even when crop is inactive. Each output/input ratio must lie in [1/8, 7/8]. Identity and enlargement are rejected. An 8x8 input may produce 1x1 output; odd output dimensions are allowed. These slide limits are stricter than general bilinear mathematics.

Both selectors select software bilinear bank zero; other banks are rejected. The deterministic PC-generated JSON is loaded and strictly validated, including its bilinear weights. Nearest and average do not use the LUT. Signed 8-bit storage, normalization 64, offsets -3..3, and phase rules are explicit software conventions, not claims about hardware bank zero. The public Linux driver explicitly identifies Q4.20 scaling; interpreting its packed coefficient bytes as signed values suggests normalization 64 (an inference). See https://codebrowser.dev/linux/linux/drivers/media/platform/arm/mali-c55/mali-c55-resizer.c.html.

The screenshot labels its last set-15/phase-31 rows as 511 and 512. The stated 16 sets x 32 phases x 2 words instead implies 1024 words, indexed 0-1023. Under sequential packing, word0=64*set+2*phase and word1=word0+1; the final pair would be 1022/1023. This arithmetic is an inference, not a correction to verified hardware documentation.
The hfilt_tinc screenshot describes horizontal input/output heights. The wrapper uses widths, consistent with the horizontal axis and width_in/owidth.

Coordinate and validation arithmetic use unbounded Python integers. Pixel intermediates use int64; the nonnegative normalized bilinear bank bounds horizontal sums by 16320 and vertical sums by 1044480. Average sums are at most 1020. A C port must bound dimensions and choose widths for coordinate state, shifts, and addresses. Hardware equivalence requires verified phases, coefficients, intermediate precision, rounding, boundaries, formats, and limits.

Repeated integer addition adds no rounding error absent overflow. With delta=T/2^20-input/output, coordinate drift is u*delta for original mapping and (u+1/2)*delta for shift. Nearest-even phase selection adds at most 1/64 input pixel relative to the programmed coordinate, without feeding back into the accumulator. The phase diagnostic command writes exact-coordinate CSV traces and a summary of separate errors. Runtime retains at most seven filtered rows (at most two for these kernels); image decoding/collection and clock-cycle handshakes are outside that buffer bound.
